record.paper_title: Tiling by translates of a function: results and open problems
record.original_question: Does there exist a measurable set Omega contained in R with 0 < mes(Omega) < infinity and a discrete translation set Lambda contained in R with bounded density, such that either sum over lambda in Lambda of 1_Omega(x-lambda) equals 1 for almost every x, or more weakly equals some other integer level w for almost every x, with the series converging absolutely almost everywhere, and such that Lambda has no periodic structure? Here 1_Omega is the indicator function of Omega, and no periodic structure means Lambda cannot be written as a disjoint union of finitely many arithmetic progressions a_j Z + b_j with real a_j > 0 and real b_j.

evidence.quote: We say that f tiles R at level w with the translation set Lambda, or that f + Lambda is a tiling of R at level w (where w is a constant), if we have sum over lambda in Lambda of f(x - lambda) = w a.e. and the series in (1.1) converges absolutely a.e.

Does there exist a measurable set Omega subset R, 0 < mes(Omega) < +infinity, whose indicator function 1_Omega can tile at level one, or, a weaker requirement, at some other integer level w, with a translation set Lambda subset R that does not have a periodic structure?

We say that a set Lambda subset R has a periodic structure if it can be represented as a disjoint union of finitely many arithmetic progressions, namely Lambda = union from j=1 to N of (a_j Z + b_j), where a_j, b_j are real numbers and a_j > 0.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. For a measurable set $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}$ with $0<\mathrm{mes}(\Omega)<\infty$, let $\mathbf{1}_\Omega$ denote its indicator function. Let $\Lambda\subset\mathbb{R}$ be a discrete set of bounded density, i.e. $\sup_{x\in\mathbb{R}}\#(\Lambda\cap[x,x+1])<\infty$. Given a positive integer $w$, we say that $\mathbf{1}_\Omega$ tiles $\mathbb{R}$ at level $w$ with translation set $\Lambda$ if
\[
\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}\mathbf{1}_\Omega(x-\lambda)=w\qquad\text{for almost every }x\in\mathbb{R},
\]
with the series converging absolutely for almost every $x$.

We say that $\Lambda$ has a periodic structure if it can be represented as a disjoint union of finitely many arithmetic progressions
\[
\Lambda=\bigsqcup_{j=1}^{N}\bigl(a_j\mathbb{Z}+b_j\bigr),\qquad a_j>0,\; b_j\in\mathbb{R}.
\]

Question. Does there exist a measurable set $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}$ with $0<\mathrm{mes}(\Omega)<\infty$ and a discrete set $\Lambda\subset\mathbb{R}$ of bounded density, such that $\mathbf{1}_\Omega$ tiles $\mathbb{R}$ at level $1$ (or, more weakly, at some integer level $w\ge 1$) with translation set $\Lambda$, while $\Lambda$ does not have a periodic structure?
artifact.status_search_result: This is posed as an open problem in the survey on tiling by translates of a function. Recent literature (through 2024) on aperiodic tiles and the periodic tiling conjecture addresses analogous questions in $\mathbb{Z}^d$ and higher-dimensional $\mathbb{R}^d$, but no resolution for indicator functions of bounded measurable subsets of $\mathbb{R}$ with bounded-density translation sets has been reported. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Tiling by translates of a function: results and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing open problems including whether an indicator set of finite measure can tile R at an integer level with a non-periodic bounded-density translation set.
status_evidence.claim: The question is explicitly listed as an open problem in this survey.

status_evidence.title: Tiling, Spectrality and Aperiodicity of Connected Sets
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work (2023-2024) on aperiodic translational tiles in higher dimensions; does not resolve the one-dimensional indicator-tiling question.
status_evidence.claim: No resolution of the one-dimensional aperiodic indicator-tiling problem is reported.
